utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we take the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Alexis Demirdjian, Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zecevic, we've been alerted by the Court Officer that there's some matters that you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I haven't been in contact, of course, with the witnesses or VWS, so I'm not aware if the witness is told or made aware that he should come back. Now, what I wanted to suggest was that Your Honours inform him about that -- that's the fact right now as I see it, that he will need to come back, so he can over the breaks he can maybe think about the dates which might -- he might be unavailable so we can properly schedule that. That is the only thing I wanted to raise. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Did I [Microphone not activated] -- hear correctly yesterday when counsel were making their comments that apart from the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the presiding judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thanks. Did I correctly gather yesterday that from the comments that counsel made that apart from the witness's personal convenience with the firm fixture you have for your experts with the very earliest that he would be available would be the week beginning the -- the very earliest that we would be get back to him would be the 23rd of May? As I said, we still have to find out what his convenience is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, Ms. Korner and myself, we were just discussing that before the -- before the start of the session. There might be a possibility that we can hear this witness on the week of 16th already after we finish the experts. Now, that -- of course, that depends on the length of the cross-examination because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- and the other arguments that we can anticipate are going to be heard in the court. Or maybe we can -- maybe we can also schedule him to start as early as the 2nd of May and move the expert. What is the -- the situation with the expert is the following: I explained to Your Honours, it needs to be finished for Mr. Bajagic in the month of May. That's our concern. Because after that he starts the examinations and all that that then he might not be available until end of -- before the summer break. That's why we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course, best case scenario is that if Ms. Korner requires 20 hours that's five sitting days, so that's the week of the 2nd gone already and that may very well create problems for you. But what I propose to do is when the witness comes into court today to alert him to the problem so he can think about it, and when we rise tomorrow - because we are going to be back here tomorrow - if he is in a position to communicate to VWS any problems that he has, then we'll know where to go from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So could we have the witness back on the stand, please. Sorry, Ms. Korner, before I put the question to the witness, picking up on my last comment about your 20 hours, is it safe to say that if you were to begin on the 2nd of May, there may very well have to be an interruption so probably that may not be the prudent option?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When Your Honour says "interruption," sorry, do you mean that if I started on the 2nd and I went over the week or -- well, Your Honour mentioned interruption, what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, because I'm thinking of the problem with Mr. Zecevic's expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I certainly -- yes, it would certainly cause a problem if I had to interrupt my cross-examination. There's no question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So probably --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I would suggest it's probably safer to go for the later date rather than -- and have Mr. Zecevic -- I'm sorry, I don't know [indiscernible] Mr. Zecevic's name, Mr. Zecevic start his expert and deal with it then. I actually thought because Mr. Zecevic said that he had 15 hours with his expert, that the likelihood was that the expert would take a couple of weeks, or the best part, but Mr. Zecevic now says he is probably not going to take that length of time. But I think it's probably -- let's deal with the experts as arranged and then we'll go back to Mr. Whatever his name is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Bjelosevic. You may take your seat. Before Mr. Zecevic resumes his examination-in-chief, there is a procedural matter on which the Chamber is inviting your input, and it is this: You would recall that at the beginning of your testimony I alerted you as to the estimated lengths of time that counsel altogether would take. The result of the progress we are making is that with the holiday weekend that is about to begin and for certain administrative reasons, a decision was taken several months ago that it would not be practical to sit in the three available sitting days next week. Your testimony is not going to be completed within this week. Now, the Chamber appreciates that notwithstanding your obligation to the Chamber and to the Tribunal to attend as a witness having been summoned that as is the case with all witnesses it is not a personally convenient thing to have to attend court and it presents some disruption in your ordinary schedule. What we have to decide is this: Because of arrangements that are in place in respect of other witnesses who Mr. Zecevic is calling, that when your examination-in-chief by Mr. Zecevic and your cross-examination by Mr. Krgovic on behalf of the accused Zupljanin is completed this week, that counsel for the Prosecution, Ms. Korner, would not begin her cross-examination of you until you return. Now, I mentioned earlier the arrangements that are in place in respect of other witnesses, and it appears that the earliest that we would be able to return to you is -- there's an outside chance of the week beginning the 16th of May, but more likely than not the 23rd of May, so if you would bear those dates in mind and give it some thought in the course of today and over night, and when we take the adjournment tomorrow I would raise this matter with you again and your either then or at some -- in the days following, if you could communicate directly with the Victims and Witnesses Section of the Tribunal to let us know how your -- what dates would cause the leasts disruption in your own schedule. Do you understand the question that I'm posing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand and yesterday I heard a bit about that. It seemed that I would be coming back. The most convenient date for me would be the 9th of May, but that's not a date that you offered, so I'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zecevic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, let us continue from where we broke off yesterday. We were discussing Bosanski Samac and the situation towards the end of November in Bosanski Samac. I would like us to look at the document in tab 185. The document is 262D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 185. Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a dispatch. It's roughly the 23rd or 25th of November, 1992. It was sent to the public security station of Bosanski Samac and it is signed by chief of the centre Andrija Bjelosevic. Can you confirm to us that this is your dispatch, or actually can you tell us whether this is your dispatch, whether it was sent to Bosanski Samac, and what was the reason for sending it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a dispatch of the CSB. I sent the document and signed it. It was sent to the public security station of Samac with the request of having the chief of that station at the time, Stevan Todorovic to report immediately to the minister or assistant minister, Tomo Kovac. If we recall everything that had preceded this particular date, then the arrest of Todorovic by the security organs of the military, many omissions in the work of this public security station in the previous period, and I also wish to recall the dispatch I sent to the minister and the president of the republic. So it was after all of that that conditions were created for this, for having Stevan Todorovic dismissed from that position of chief of the public security station. That is why he was supposed to report immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have the testimony, do we need it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a look at 270, D1, tab 188. Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document without a date. On page 3 there's signature, Mirko Blazanovic compiled the report, or wrote the report, and there's his signature there as well. The subject of this document is the activities of the activity co-ordination work group in the Samac public security station. What is written here is that it's addressed to the Republika Srpska MUP in Bijeljina. Tell me, do you know about this document? Who was Mirko Blazanovic? Tell us everything you can about this document, whatever you may know.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already mentioned this name. Mirko Blazanovic was the chief of the department of the milicija in the CSB Doboj from the month of June onwards. This is indeed his signature, I can recognise it, and this is a document that was written up after the visit of a group that was sent on the 27th of November, 1992, sent to Samac. They looked at the work of the public security station to that date and they noticed many flagrant omissions. I would like to underline that, flagrant omissions, and they are listed here. The station area had not been divided into patrolling sectors and areas in the building without any appropriate decision. 41 persons were being held in detention of five different ethnic backgrounds as it is stated here, so the Samac public security station did not observe the decision of the ministry. The date was the 10th of August. That was a surprise for that group that was staying there, that group of inspectors, and for all of us as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move the English text a bit so that everyone can follow what the witness is saying. It's the same page but could you just go to the bottom of the page. Perhaps the next page would be required as well, I couldn't see it myself. I do apologise. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Bjelosevic, for having interrupted you, but this is necessary for all the other participants to be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. So let me move on, let me state what was observed. No records were being kept, and I remember when contacting the commander Savo Cancarevic that question had been raised once, namely that he even interfered in assignments given by the service. So it wasn't the komandir or his deputy that did that but he did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, when you say "he," who is he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to Stevan Todorovic because he is the person we are discussing. Then the operative coverage of the station's territory was very poor. The negligence towards equipment, all of this is specifically noted. I'm underlining the word "flagrant" once again, flagrant omissions in the work of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me about the signature, are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a copy of this document? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The centre received a copy and the situation was discussed and it is Mirko Blazanovic's signature, no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D519, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Another document that has to do with the same matter, 268D1, 189, that is the tab number. Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a dispatch dated the 27th of November, 1992. It says CSB Doboj on the top of the page and then your name rather is at the bottom of the page by way of a signature, and then there's something that was added here, something handwritten. This dispatch was sent to the MUP of Republika Srpska, to the minister, and to the commander of the special purpose police. That is the brigade of the Special Police attached to the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm this for us? Is this your document? What was the reason for sending this document, and can you tell us what happened in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is a document of the CSB Doboj indeed. I sent this dispatch. May I just say what the reason was, although you can see it from the text of the document itself? After all the things that happened beforehand and that we have discussed already, Stevan Todorovic tried to win over the milicija and some members of the military and -- to oppose his dismissal. The security situation in the territory, the municipality of Samac had already become increasingly complex. I told you already that an inspector had been sent there, and he monitored the situation as it was. That's why I asked the minister to send reinforcements there from the Special Police, that is. As you can see that this document was also sent to Milenko Karisik, commander of the special purpose police. This request was indeed met. I see this handwritten text on the top of the page and it says that a work group was sent to Samac and then further on it says Saric, that was Goran Saric, if I remember correctly, he was an inspector of the milicija in the department at the MUP headquarters, then Ostoja the crime department. It's probably Ostoja Minic, and he was indeed on that team. After that Stevan Todorovic quite simply left the public security station. He went to the municipality and he did something there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D520, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, on the English translation, there is another piece of information that has been translated. "The work details report says that there is no need to send the unit." Mr. Bjelosevic, but you say that there was a unit sent to Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure at that additional forces were sent there at that time. I don't remember their number. And I know that they were accompanied by Marinko Djukic, an inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, what is translated here as a work detail, "a work detail has been sent to Samac" and then "the work details report says that there is no need to sent a unit." What is meant by "a work detail"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the handwritten text?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, a detail or a group or a team means that there was a group of people sent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps the witness can read what is written in Serbian so it can be translated by interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, could you read aloud the handwritten notation at the top, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm starting from the top: "A work group has been sent to Samac." I can't read the last word, I'm not sure. And then later on it says Saric, after a little dash, Saric was an inspector of milicija from the headquarters of MUP, and then it says Ostoja crime department, he was an inspector from the crime prevention department, Ostoja Milic [as interpreted]. And then "the work group's report says that there is no need to send a unit." And then there's somebody's signature, maybe Zuban but I'm not sure, but I'm sure that a unit was sent at approximately that time. Maybe a little bit before or a little bit after, and I know that Marinko Djukic, an inspector from the Security Services Centre of Doboj accompanied them. That was a group that had been in the army before that, and I don't know in which unit, and their leader was an individual nicknamed Ljapo. They went towards the station, and I know for sure that a unit was sent there and spent some time there as reinforcement and then the situation calmed down. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe if you permit me one more explanation. Maybe these are people from Doboj. Maybe this unit came from Doboj, but they were there, I remember that very well. They went there because of the attempt on part of that Ljapo to take over the station. I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I have another query on this document. Mr. Bjelosevic, having regard to the content of the -- what the original document says, that the classification initially is that it was not urgent, is there an inconsistency there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here "DX," yes, but I really don't know why it wasn't marked as very urgent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just an issue about the transcript. 12/1, when you were reading out the name Ostoja, you said something and then in the transcript it ended up Ostoja Milic, can you repeat the surname?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ostoja Minic. As far as I remember, his surname is Minic and not Milic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D60, tab 175.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this is a document originating at the Ministry of the Interior in Bijeljina. The date is 16th of November, 1992. On page 3 we can see typed Minister Mico Stanisic as well as signature and a stamp. On page 1 there is some handwritten text. My first question, are you familiar with this document and did you receive it at the time, and if you did, what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the document. It's about the conclusions adopted at the collegium meeting on the 5th of November in Bijeljina. This document was sent to us in the field and it contained a more detailed description of the conclusions adopted at the collegium meeting. It also contains more details about the procedure for nominating personnel for certain positions in the National Security Service and public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, it doesn't matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 258D1, tab 177.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document originating at the department for police duties and assignments. It's an activity plan. It contains three signatures. Can you first explain the first page out of four pages in this document. Is this your document and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document originating in the Doboj Security Services Centre. In the milicija department or police department there was an inspector and a long time ago it also used to be a department in charge of organisation and mobilisation. At the time of this document, these affairs were handled by Rajko Bilic, an inspector. If you remember yesterday we spoke about the problems related to the criteria for the members of the reserve police. Having noticed the aforementioned problems, this inspector drafted his work-plan or activity plan. It was approved by the chief of sector Mirko Stojcinovic, and I authorised the plan. This inspector visited police stations in the territory of the centre and then reported about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we take a look at the second page and then you can explain that page. We can see a signature of Rajko Bilic. So what is this report about, can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I again have to go back to what we discussed yesterday, and that is although there were very clear orders, instructions, and warnings, still there were still some problems in some of the stations. Here we can see that Inspector Bilic, while working in accordance with his plan that had been approved and authorised, went to the SJB in Doboj and found that five members of the reserve police were people who did not serve the usual national service in the army. On top of that, there were five other people that had been convicted of crimes which rendered them unsuitable for their jobs. And now if you take a look at the date, and if we know that warnings to resolve this situation were issued as early as August, then we see that this is a clear obstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain pages 3 and 4, the two lists.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These lists form a part of the report drafted by Inspector Bilic. He made a separate list of the members of the SJB Doboj that had been convicted listing their names, courts that had convicted them, and criminal offences, or more precisely, numbers of relevant articles. So here we can see their names. And on the following page, there's also a list and it's also part of the report drafted by Inspector Bilic and this list contains the names of the members of the reserve force of milicija in the Doboj SJB who had not regulated their military service. And that was one of the criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D521, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 45D1. 45D1, tab 178A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a dispatch by Minister Stanisic from the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. The date is the 20th of November, 1992. It was sent to Municipal Assemblies. Here it says "everyone" and I don't know whether that pertains to all municipalities or Security Services Centre. Are you familiar with this document? Have you received it? And if yes, can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of this document. The minister sent this document to all the municipalities in the territory of the Serbian republic. I emphasise that there had been long discussions spread over several collegium meetings relating to the desire of the local authorities and the local politicians to appoint their own people, people chosen by them, people who were loyal to them. Although the nomination procedure was very clear, Minister Stanisic had told us, chiefs of centres, that three candidates should be nominated for the position of the chief of the station in consultation with local authorities, however local authorities thought that that was insufficient for their purposes. We consulted them about certain people, but they wouldn't want any of those people. They would tell us we want this particular person on this position. That's why this document was sent. In this document, the minister speaks directly to the presidents of Municipal Assemblies and Executive Boards and he tells them how this should be done, and the document was also sent to us for information. And only from that point on the pressure was slightly lesser than before. I mean, the pressure exerted by the local authorities, but it did not completely disappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D522, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 259D1, tab 179.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, is this your document? It says here chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is a dispatch which was sent to the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka. It was to be given to Vojo Kupresanin, and there is also an explanation in here as to why the dispatch was being sent. As you can see from the dispatch contents, at 1300 hours in front of the police social centre in Doboj on the 22nd of November, 1992, deputies from the parliament of Republika Srpska gathered. They were escorted because the area of the corridor was not safe at the time. It was rather unsafe. It was exposed to daily artillery fire. Very often groups appeared there and engaged in short attacks and then withdrew towards what was then the enemy side. That's why the deputies had to be escorted, for their safety. They had to be escorted to their destination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I've shown you this document precisely to show an example which would help us explain what was the meaning of escort. Escorting somebody as an action carried out by the police?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Escorting can take place under different circumstances. In peacetime, this usually means escorting people in order to secure a safe passage through traffic and similar exceptional conditions. However, under the conditions when this happened, it was war time and the situation was very complex. The activity was therefore also very complex and had to be carried out with full responsibility by the security organs. We had to secure the route of their movement through the corridor. The route had to be additionally secured by the police who were placed there to observe the situation. The column had an armed escort as well at the beginning and the end of the column in case of attack. Those armed escorts were prepared to engage and to ensure a secure movement of vehicles and safety for the deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, was this an activity that the Ministry of the Interior was authorised to carry out in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 1D321, currently marked for identification, tab 182.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a two-page document. The first page is a cover letter. I believe that the date is the 25th November, 1992. It was sent to all public security stations by the Security Services Centre in Doboj, and the signature is chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic. Kindly tell us briefly whether this is your document, what was it about, who was it sent to and why?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a cover letter which was sent to all the public security stations in the Doboj Security Services Centre area. I signed the document. As you can see enclosure 1 is the directive on maintaining storage deposits which was sent by the Ministry of the Interior. The minister had signed it, and here in the top right-hand side corner you can see the word "copy." We received the directive from the minister and then we made a sufficient number of the copies thereof and sent them to the public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document was marked for identification because the previous witness was not in a position to authorise it, or rather, recognise it. Since this witness has just confirmed that this document was drafted by him, I would like to the MFI marking to be removed from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We could do that, Mr. Zecevic, but I confess I'm at a loss as to why this -- what appears to be a routine piece of correspondence would have been entered even provisionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are going to be asking about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. So we would de-MFI it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 46D1, tab 193.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, I have to make it clear why I said that. You only saw the front page of that. There is three pages to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not following.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When asked -- when I said -- Their Honours, when they were asking you about the last document that you wanted de-MFI'd, all that was on the thing was the front page. It's actually a three-page document, that's what I was explaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but I didn't want to show all three pages because the document has been already admitted, only it's been MFI'd due to the fact that the authenticity was -- could not have been established by the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That was all for my edification, Mr. Zecevic. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a letter, or rather, a dispatch bearing the date 3rd December, 1992. It was sent from the crime prevention administration in Bijeljina and sent to the Doboj CSB. And they are referring to your report dated the 6 November 1992, and we can see that something was added by hand. I believe that it is a family name. Are you familiar with this document, and can you briefly explain what the document is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this dispatch. It arrived from the crime prevention administration at the seat of the MUP. This dispatch is connected with one of our documents. I believe that we saw it in this courtroom earlier and in that dispatch we wanted a search warrant to be issued for certain vehicles and property stolen from the company Krivaja based in Zavidovici, and this is the administration's response. The dispatch was signed by the then chief of the administration or perhaps the assistant chief, Goran Macar. What is added by hand is the marking of the crime prevention department and it was delivered to Branislav Petricevic who at the time was the head of that department, or rather, the head of the economic crime department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The MUP of the Republika Srpska, the crime prevention administration hereby informs you about what?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the administration will take measures necessary to locate the stolen property and goods which were stolen in our centre and transported to the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since this document refers your dispatch that we already commented upon, would you say that this was an example showing the functioning along the lines of work?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. This is what it reflects. Perhaps you will remember another dispatch sent by the ministry, or rather, by the minister. It had to do with the correspondence with the neighbouring MUPs. It seems that the MUP here has already entered in a correspondence with their counter-part in another republic and they are just sending us a letter for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a crime prevention administration at the CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a department and within that department there was a section for economic crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just explain. At the level of Security Services Centres were there departments or were there administrations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administration existed at the level of the ministry. We had departments. For example, we had -- the MUP had the administration for policing, the administration for crime prevention, the administration for administrative and legal affairs and so on and so forth. And then that hierarchy along the lines of work came down to the centres, and then in the centres there were departments which corresponded to each of the administrations in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This means that an administration existed at the MUP, a department existed at the CSB, and what did the public security station have?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time the public security stations had sections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D523, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is this document -- no, no, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is related to one previous document which the witness was talking about. [Interpretation] The document is in connection with 1D488. Can the witness please be shown 274D1, tab 195.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document in whose heading you see the Security Services Centre Doboj. The date is the 3rd December 1992. There is a typed up signature of chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic, but I believe that there is a word "for" and another signature. Can you explain what the document is about, whether the document was assigned under your authority, did you know about it, what does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document originates from the Security Services Centre in Doboj, and it is about measures and tasks ordered to the police station in Petrovo. Those measures and tasks had arisen from the control and instructive inspection which was carried out at the station. It had been established that certain omissions were made and there were shortcomings in the work of the station and it was immediately ordered that those shortcomings should be eliminated. The shortcomings that were noted are listed in here, dead-lines are given, and this document was signed by the chief of the public security sector, Mirko Stojcinovic. He was authorised by me to sign certain documents including this one. As you can see, there are immediate dead-lines. Some tasks are described as on-going and for some tasks there is a dead-line of several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no objections, but I wonder if the witness could read paragraph 2 in the Serbian language because the English translation doesn't make much sense at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Establish records on the use of means of coercion and ensure lawful procedure in cases of use of means of coercion."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. Zecevic wants to ask Mr. Bjelosevic what that refers to, because I don't want to have to come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a problem with the translation. Could you explain what means of coercion are. What is meant by that? Could you please explain what it is that is referred to in paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to remind you that we have already discussed this and that this is what the procedure is: If a person who violated the law have certain measures taken against him or her, that involves a certain procedure, certain rules as to how this takes place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say certain measures, could you please explain the measures involved?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to explain now. First there is an order, an order can be issued to the effect of come with us, but then you have to assess the situation. You see, the situation is assessed each and every time. What kind of person is involved, is this person going to put up a resistance, will this person draw a fire-arm, for instance, and then measures are planned on that basis, and then there's a gradual process. The resistance can be active or passive. If it's passive, again there has to be coercion involved, the person has to be brought to a vehicle if necessary. If there is a court order to bring that person into custody if the person was caught while committing a crime and if there is a tendency to the effect that this person may continue doing that, then the person may be tied up in order to be brought in. Also a truncheon may be used, a rubber one. And in most drastic cases when lives are threatened either of the policeman or of other citizens, then even fire-arms can be used. All of these measures that are applied have to be recorded, described. That's the way it was at the time as well. If physical force was used to overcome a person, then the policeman when handing over that individual has to describe what he did, so this report, whatever it had to do with, physical strength, tying a person up, et cetera, all of that has to be recorded. All of these means of coercion have to be described, recorded, and then it is the superior that determines how justified that was. I don't know whether it was clear, everything I have been explaining so far. What has been noted here is that not all reports were made and then an order was issued to have the situation addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that the witness explained this in an exhaustive fashion and if there are no further questions, I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I understand his explanation to date, but there's one small point. I understand fully the record keeping part of it, but this ensure lawful procedure in cases, does this -- the lawful procedure, is it the record keeping or is this lawful procedure a detailed, for want of a better expression, escalation, if the suspect does this you can only do that and so on? Do you understand my question? The latter part of that when you say is ensure lawful procedure. You are nodding your head, what's your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. It is never superfluous to note certain things. When instructions are being issued, when measures are being ordered, et cetera. My understanding of this was simply to redress this lack that was noted in the records and then also to ensure lawful procedure when means of coercion are applied. That is never superfluous. It's always a good idea to remind policemen of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, the question was as follows, if I may be of assistance: Is there a procedure involved as to when and in which cases which measure of coercion may be applied? That is the first question. So could you please respond to that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is regulated in the rules on the work and conduct of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do these rules envisage the cases in which a member of the police has the right to use a rubber truncheon, physical force, or fire-arms, and are the situations involved specified?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of this was elaborated in the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic. The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D524, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one document before the break, could the witness please be shown 48D1. That is document 217A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document entitled "Instruction on Record Keeping in Police Stations." I would like to know whether you are familiar with this, whether you had received it, under which circumstances, who issued these instructions, and could you specifically comment on paragraph 7 on page 6?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document entitled "Instruction on Record Keeping in Police Stations." The document came from the Ministry of the Interior and this is paragraph 7 that refers precisely to that, recording the use of force, means of coercion and that is elaborated here. And you see it refer to gradually, as I said, how this should be applied. Then this book is a record of the use of physical force, a rubber baton, fire-arms, and other means of restraint while performing duty. That's it. So when the document said that there was a lawful procedure involved, it meant this record keeping as well because that is something that was prescribed too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were the effects of the use recorded too, the effects of the use of one of these means of coercion?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There are special boxes for recording all of that. First of all the number, and then what was used and then what the effects were. We can read it out if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There's no need for that. The document is self-explanatory. Could you just explain to us, I mean from a technical point of view, justification of the use of force, how was that assessed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the means that were used. After the report would be written up and after the circumstances were established, how the particular means of coercion were applied for physical force, rubber baton, it was the chief of the police -- the public security station that assessed how justified that was, but it was the head of the CSB that assessed whether it was justified to use a fire-arm. And then what was ultimately established was that this was used in a justified or unjustified manner. In my own practice or career, I had both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If it is assessed that it was unjustified, what would happen then?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then disciplinary measures are taken depending on the consequences or effects that followed, even criminal proceedings could have been instituted. And actually, in some cases, it's obligatory to institute criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D525, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see the time, perhaps it would be a convenient moment to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we rise and resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one matter while the usher is bringing the witness in, concerns the interpretation because we see that there has been two interpretations of this particular subject that we were discussing with the witness. One was coercion and the other was use of force. Now, I discussed with Ms. Korner and Ms. Korner advised me that coercion in English would be considered as unlawful use of force and basically what the witness was talking about is the use of force during arrest. So I just wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That was certainly the sense with which I was left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree. It became, as Mr. Zecevic just said, if you discuss it coercion used in English suggests an unlawful use of force which is why I raised it because that's why it looked so odd. And I agree entirely that when he gave the explanation what he was clearly explaining, and I think it's common with police forces in most countries, is that if you use force, even lawful force, during the course of an arrest, you have to record that somewhere, and I accept that that's entirely what is meant by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are just waiting. Having discussed the matter over the break again, we think probably the 16th of May would be the appropriate time for Mr. Bjelosevic to return. And it may be rather than to-ing and fro-ing between him and VWS, he should be asked if that week would cause him any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I'll ask him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And one other matter, Your Honour, 1D514 was MFI'd because of the revised translation. The revised translation was received and it has been uploaded. So 1D514 should be de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, the MFI status on that -- qualification on that is lifted. Mr. Bjelosevic, before we resume, further on the matter to which I alerted you at the beginning, having heard from counsel during the break, it looks as if the 16th of May is a feasible date for you to return, so when you would have thought about it, you can confirm to us before we take the adjournment tomorrow whether that would present any insurmountable problems for you. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, a few more questions on the topic we discussed before the break. You said that the chief of the Security Services Centre is the person who decides whether the use of fire-arms was justified. How is the chief of the Security Services Centre informed about the use of fire-arms, can you explain how it went on in practice?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you an example. Something that happened in the territory of the public security station of Petrovo. Fire-arms were used by a policeman. In such a case, both the centre and the MUP have to be informed about it urgently, then a commission is formed to perform an on-site investigation. In this particular example, the consequence was death of a person. Investigative judge also has to be informed for purposes of his investigation. However, in parallel with his investigation, a report on the use of force has to be compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who writes this report?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who used force writes this report. The chief of station attaches his opinion but the final judgement about whether the use was justified rests with the chief of the centre. In this particular case, I judged based on information contained in the report that the use of fire-arm was unjustified. This policeman was suspended, criminal proceedings were instigated against him, and he was convicted because it was considered a criminal offence. So this is an example of an unjustified use of fire-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking about chiefs of centres, is there a duty to inform you as the chief of centre about every such instance of use of fire-arms by members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When police performs combat tasks, is the situation the same, do they still have the same duty?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, when they perform combat tasks, military rules are in force. Under these circumstances, it is not necessary to report about every individual case. When the unit returns, a memo is drafted containing information that the unit was engaged in combat tasks, where, how long, consequences for the unit, if any, casualties, killed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, you actually answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have now 290D1. Tab 216.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date is the 31st December, 1992. It is addressed to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, in parentheses Doboj section. On the right-hand side we see chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic and the signature, and on the left-hand side there is a stamp, a signature, and the confirmation of receipt. Can you tell us, is this your document and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document originating in the Doboj Security Services Centre. I signed it. This is a request that certain individuals should be put on work obligation at the time they were engaged in the Doboj CSB. According to the regulations that were in force at the time, individuals who worked in certain institutions and organs and who were supposed to be assigned to those positions by the Ministry of Defence, all that had to be done through their particular sections. In this particular case, this is the Doboj section.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think you already mentioned it, but can you remind us, who kept the documentation on military conscripts and what war time roster was the roster that these individuals were supposed to be included in?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documentation on military conscripts was kept by the Ministry of Defence in their respective sections in the field. They decided about individual assignments, whether somebody would be sent to a war unit or work obligation. In this case, request is made for these individuals to be sent to work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Work obligation where?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Work obligation here in the police social centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D526, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 286D1, tab 209.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the letterhead is Security Services Centre Doboj. The date is the 23rd December 1992. On the second page we see chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic and the signature. Can you confirm that this is your document and can you explain what it is about and why it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document originates in the Doboj Security Services Centre. I signed it. As you can see, it's a draft decision on establishing which employees of the Ministry of the Interior are considered authorised officials. This document was the basis for a discussion. Opinions were invited before the definitive version of the appropriate regulation could be established. As you can see, it was sent to all the public security stations in the field, it says here "all."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So was a decision made, a final decision, on which employees are to be considered authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a discussion and as far as I can remember there were some suggestions that were sent to the ministry, and after that the final regulation was enacted by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What are we supposed to conclude from this document, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe -- Your Honours, I believe the matter is of certain significance. Namely, this shows who -- which members of the Ministry of the Interior are to considered authorised officials. And you will see during the course of our expert testimony what are the prerogatives, so to speak, of the authorised officials. And if you remember, there has been a number of times that we discussed whether the members of the Ministry of the Interior when resubordinated to the army maintain their position or their authority as authorised officials or not, and that is a matter of dispute, as I understand, between the parties in this case. That is why we believe -- that is why we believe this document is important. I'm just reminded that there has been a certain discussion on the same subject, authorised officials, on page 3696 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But if I understand the testimony correctly, this -- document that we now have was a discussion paper, discussions followed, and the result was an actual regulation which I would expect, to the extent it is relevant, to have migrated into the law library. Why would we need the discussion paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, what is contained in the law library is the documents which were taken or accepted by the MUP of RS and they were created by MUP of BiH, so throughout the -- this period from April until December the documents which were regulating this matter were the ones from the MUP of BiH. Now, this document is dated 23rd of December and it shows that the MUP of RS was -- was deciding on the matter or actually taking the position within the structure on this particular matter by end of the year. And we believe it's relevant to show that the Ministry of the Interior of RS is conducting this procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But could I just ask then a follow-up question to the issue that was just raised by the presiding judge, namely, does this decision in its draft or in its final form actually address the issue of the functions during re-subordination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because the functions during re-subordinations are regulated by other laws. This only concerns what are the authorities of the authorised official and who the authorised officials within the Ministry of the Interior are. And that is regulated by the regulation of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, maybe I'm missing something, but the difficulty that I still have is that what we now have before us is, as it were, step one. It would be the result of this exercise that we would find useful, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I question that because as Mr. Zecevic rightly says, the applicable law during the period that we are considering in this indictment is that which was still -- is still that which applied to the old BiH MUP. The discussions they were having, nothing came into effect until 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, I do agree with Ms. Korner. This -- the result of this procedure which was conducted in the end of 1992 was -- it resulted in the document which was -- which was published only in 1993, therefore, outside of the scope of the indictment. But, Your Honours, our position is that we need to show that the Ministry of the Interior of RS was conducting each and every step in order to establish the functions of the Ministry of the Interior as it should be according to the law throughout 1992. And that is the importance of this document, as well as the importance which I already stated about the rights of the authorised officials and the position during the re-subordination to the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is it possible that one reading this document could be misled as to who constitutes -- who falls in this category of authorised officials, that's my concern? That we have this proposal but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I must say that I never thought about it that way and I'm grateful for Your Honours to raise it. I can't guarantee that because it might be, as witness just testified, that there has been some proposals, and we don't know whether these proposals were accepted or not and I accept -- I accept fully that intervention and therefore I agree, I will withdraw my proposal to tender this document because the last thing I would need is to mislead the Trial Chamber on anything, especially on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it occurs to me there may be one other simple question to ask, and that's whether there is any difference between who was an authorised official under this proposal and that under the law which they were operating under throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I think as we have that in the law library and we have the expert witness coming, I can ask the witness this question but still it wouldn't change the position on this document, I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand that, but it may be useful to get this witness's response to that particular question in as much as he was working with --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Mr. Bjelosevic, please. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, one question, we see that this was sent on the 23rd of December. Which regulations were applied before December 1992 to regulate these issues?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially what applied was the organisation that was in effect within the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Later on it was regulated more in the territory of public station, and I would say that it was on a case-by-case basis. And when the ministry was established and when this communications system was established, things became more regulated, certain proposals were sought from the public security stations, they were sent to the centre and finally from the centres they would be forwarded and regulations were drafted that I considered final and applicable in the future period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: According to the regulations that were in effect in the former ministry in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the persons listed in this proposal, did they enjoy the status of authorised personnel in keeping with the law, can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time there were similarities in terms of who could be considered an authorised person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there were similarities, you have to be more precise. Do you know what the differences were, how did the two differ?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The differences as far as I can remember were regulated by the regulations that state security service was separated from the centres and it became a special service. When the regulation was drafted in Bosnia-Herzegovina within the centres, there was a sector of public as well as the sector of state security. The rest in practical terms was police officers, crime inspectors and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bjelosevic, could you please focus. We are not talking about the division into public as opposed to state security. I'm talking about the status of authorised personnel within the Ministry of the Interior. My question was this: The persons listed in the proposal under Roman I and II and III as well, as far as you can remember, according to the regulations that were applicable to the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did the same persons or individuals enjoy the status of authorised persons or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If there were any differences, what did the differences consist of? What did they constitute?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure whether this would be applicable to the communications centre employees. I believe that that was the only difference. Everything else is practically the same starting with the ministers, deputy assistants, chiefs of centres, chiefs of public security stations and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say communications centre employees, what are you saying? What do you mean by that? Are you saying that communication centre employees under the law in effect and applicable by the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were they authorised individuals or were they not and then that's changed so they became authorised persons, can you explain?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the regulations that were applied during the existence of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the communications centre employees were also authorised persons. I know that there was a discussion during that period about the status of those persons and that it became clear that authorised persons could be only those persons who apply authorisations. The communication centre employees were not in that category and that's why it was proposed that communication centres employees would no longer figure as authorised personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether the witness's answer has been of assistance to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. Thanks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this mean that the Trial Chamber perhaps now has a different position then before this document was introduced, or perhaps not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have the testimony of the witness, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I appreciate it. [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 289D1, tab 214.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a CSB document dated the 30th of December, 1992. It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska to the commander of the Special Police Brigade Milenko Karisik. In the right-hand side corner it says chief of centre Andrija Bjelosevic. There seems to be a signature but I can't see it well in my copy. Could you please tell us whether this is your document, what is it about, who was it sent to and why, if this indeed is your document, if you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the document. I apologise, I'm sorry. I spoke with my family at home and I forgot to switch the phone off. I apologise. I apologise once again. It was addressed to the commander of the Special Police Brigade Milenko Karisik. Certain problems did appear in that detachment. The period was somewhat calmer, they were not so heavily engaged, and with nothing else to do, as it were, they started behaving in a manner that was not befitting a member of the Ministry of the Interior. That's why I wanted to have an urgent meeting with their commander and the detachment commander to deal with those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us why you sent this letter to the commander of the brigade, Milenko Karisik? Please tell us this first and then I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the hierarchy. The 5th Detachment was under strength of the brigade which was under the command of Mr. Milenko Karisik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Milenko Karisik their immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via the commander of the 5th Detachment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who was authorised to institute the disciplinary and other measures against them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the regulations on disciplinary responsibility, the brigade commander was the one who could do that pursuant to the detachment commander's proposal, if there were some breaches of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D527, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 282D1, tab 206. [In English] Please bear with me, Your Honours, this document might be a duplicate, so if I can have just one minute, please. [Interpretation] I have checked. It is in connection with 1D60, but we are talking about two different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bjelosevic, the document before you bears the date 17 December 1992. On the third page -- but let me first say that this is a dispatch. On the third page you will see the typed up name of Andrija Bjelosevic but there is the word "for" and somebody else's signature. This document was sent to a certain number of security stations. Could you please confirm whether this was indeed your dispatch, what was it about, and who it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document issued by the Doboj CSB. It was addressed to the public security stations in the territory of the Doboj CSB. The purpose of this dispatch was to inform the public security stations about the new regulations on internal organisation that was coming into effect and that the previous appointments on assignment to duties and those were temporary, I believe that we saw a document in which those appointments were described as temporary. And that in keeping with the new regulations, a complete new procedure had to be carried out in order to sign personnel in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs and Regulations. And this is a reminder of the conclusions from the collegium which had taken place and the discussion that was -- that took place with regard to the new regulations and obligations arising from it. The document was signed by Mirko Stojcinovic, the chief of the public security station in the Doboj centre on behalf of the chief of centre. Of course he did it with my authorisation, I knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you tell us something about paragraph 9 on page 3 in this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the example of the control and instructive inspection in the field, you could see that there were still reservists who had criminal records or were still kept on contrary to the regulations. Paragraph 9 is another reminder that such people should not be appointed in the future, but that rather they should be excluded from the police ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We can see here that an order of the ministry is referred to in here, when was that issued?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was issued on the 23rd of July and from that time it was repeated several times by the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 17th December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D527, Your Honours. 28, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D258 [as interpreted] is the number of this document then. Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 272D1, tab 217.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document of the CSB Doboj, instructions. There is no specific date. It is just the month of December 1992. And then it says Andrija Bjelosevic, there's a stamp, that's at the end of the document. Can you explain to us whether this is your document and can you tell us what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are instructions on the conduct of the duty operations officer that were within the department of the milicija. This document is from that period, December 1992, but later on it was updated. As you can see in several positions here, if I can call it that, it -- you can see that someone used an eraser or some correcting fluid. My name was there first and then the name of Vaso Skondric was written there instead of my name. Also, as there were other personnel changes, these corrections were reflected in the same way but this really had to do with the positions that they held and this is what the duty officer did. If something happened on the ground, all the public security stations were supposed to inform the duty operations officer and in accordance with these instructions, he reported that either by applying regular procedure or an urgent procedure depending on what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just two questions. When was Vaso Skondric appointed chief of CSB Doboj, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the beginning of March, if I remember correctly, in 1994, when I became assistant head of the public security sector in accordance with the minister's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is typewritten here, is that the original text of the instruction that you signed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the instruction. I signed it and you can see that of course it was still in force at the time when I left. It was only specific information that was updated and that changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say information, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean personnel changes. I mean persons' names and surnames.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document although I do not insist, I have to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We'll admit it and mark it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D529, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It's a pity that it's only now that I realise that perhaps it's always easier to leave the decision to the Trial Chamber. I do apologise. Could the witness please be shown the next document, 276D1, 197. Tab 197.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Before we look at the document, Mr. Bjelosevic, a question. Towards the end of the day yesterday and when the first session started today we discussed the situation in Bosanski Samac. Did you take any disciplinary measures against the chief of the public security station of Bosanski Samac, Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for two reasons. Firstly, Stevan Todorovic was never appointed by a decision of the chief of the centre or of the minister of the interior. From the very outset, as we gained insight into what was going on in this public security station, I made efforts to have Todorovic dismissed from that position and that a went very slowly and with great difficulty. We saw that. After all of the problems that appeared in November when he was sent to the ministry for a discussion, he left that duty and he was not appointed to another position, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The document that we have in front of us is a document of the CSB Doboj. The date is the 8th of December, 1992. This is a decision on imposing disciplinary measure. The signature says chief of the CSB, Andrija Bjelosevic. Can you confirm that for us, can you tell us whether this is a document of yours and can you tell us what it is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this. This is a decision on imposing a disciplinary measure against a policeman of the Petrovo public security station in accordance with the rules on disciplinary responsibility. The chief of the station took the initiative and the disciplinary commission carried out the appropriate procedure and presented evidence based on the testimony of certain persons. It was established that this person had committed a disciplinary infraction. He was supposed to pay a fine amounting to 15 per cent of his monthly salary over the course of six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, just one question, in paragraph 1 this document refers to the rules on disciplinary responsibility of employees of the MUP in conditions of a war time regimen. Do you remember what the difference was between that set of rules and the rules on disciplinary responsibility envisaged by the law on the interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
